name: issue_827_hot_day_deadband_cleared_escalates
description: Issue #827 / #1066 (Design D nearest-edge arming, docs/08-COMPUTATION-REFERENCE.md section 6f). A genuine cold snap on a hot-classified day: indoor drops from 71F to 61F, 7F below comfort_heat(68). The first evaluation below the floor (06:15) arms heat and commands it; the hot-day classification does not matter. Originally the 'escalates past the deadband' half of a pair with the dawn-dip case; under #1066 both halves arm heat on the first breach reading and differ only in how far below the floor indoor is.
source: Issue #827 Design table, deadband table 'Hot' row -- companion positive case to the within-deadband negative control.
notes: Occupant impact: a 61F house on a day the forecast calls hot still needs heat. The occupant must not coast 7F below the floor waiting for a confirmation.

Design D rule exercised (docs/08 section 6f): indoor < floor -> heating immediately on any day type. The 06:17 re-evaluation is a redundant re-affirmation kept from the original timeline; final-state assertions cannot prove WHEN heating was armed (timing evidence: issue_1066_cold_morning_mild_day_arms_heat_immediately.json). Near-duplicate of issue_827_hot_day_dawn_dip_arms_heat.json (same day type and config; breach 7F here vs 3F there, which no longer changes the outcome).

(a) Scenario effectiveness: with nearest-edge arming deleted (origin/main) a hot day is natively cooling and heat is against-grain: a 7F breach clears the hot deadband (5F) but still needs the recency check and a 90 s sustain across two evaluations. If a regression made the hot-day tier swallow a breach (for example an oversized margin or a clamp raised so a 7F breach is tolerated), comfort_family stays cooling and the final assertions fail.
(b) Docs<->production alignment: docs/08 section 6f ('Hot/cold 5F default becomes 2F ... their old extra tolerance is gone'; 'indoor < floor -> heating').
(c) Occupant outcome if this test fails to catch a regression: a real cold snap on a hot-forecast day leaves the house 7F below its comfort floor with only the AC armed.

events.note: Hot-day classification at dawn (classifier derives hvac_mode=cool, windows_recommended false). Indoor 71F is inside the band [68F, 74F].
A genuine cold snap: indoor drops to 61F, 7F below comfort_heat(68).
First evaluation with indoor below the floor: floor breach, heat is armed immediately.
Re-evaluation 2 minutes later: still below the floor, heating remains armed (redundant re-affirmation kept from the original timeline).

assertions.reason: Baseline: hot day, indoor within band -- comfort band arms normally at the ceiling.
A 7F breach arms heat despite the hot-day classification. Final-state assertion; heating was armed at the first below-floor evaluation (06:15).
The escalated mode is a real climate.set_temperature/set_hvac_mode call at comfort_heat, not merely an internal flag.

verdict.summary: A hot-classified day with a genuine 7F drop below the comfort floor arms heat on the first evaluation below the floor.
verdict.observed_behavior: Cooling family at 71F; the 61F reading at 06:15 arms heating and commands heat at comfort_heat.
verdict.expected_behavior: Below the floor always means heat, immediately, on every day type (docs/08 section 6f).
